WHAT THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS SET GOT WRONG, since the shape recurs.  `block_update's accumulator is not re-truncated` was written as `acc + ((x[j] * hist[idx]) & 0xffff)` and came back NOT CAUGHT -- correctly, because masking a term to 16 bits before adding it to a value that is itself narrowed to `short` on assignment is congruent modulo 65536 and agrees on every input.  It attacked nothing.  The truncation is carried by the DECLARATION plus the cast together, so the mutation now spans both lines and widens `acc` to `int` AND drops the cast in one edit; it is caught.  A mutation that survives because it is a no-op is worse than no mutation, because it reads as a measured gap.

lmsupd2's second stage shifts by 18, as the single-stage form does
block_update's circular wrap is a modulo rather than one conditional add
block_update accumulates in 32 bits instead of re-truncating each iteration
why: PROVED UNOBSERVABLE, AND THE PROOF IS SHORT.  By induction the two accumulators are congruent modulo 65536 at every step: the 16-bit one is trunc16(acc + p) and the wide one is acc + p, and trunc16 is the identity modulo 65536.  Everything downstream is linear over that modulus -- `acc` is used once, in `(short)(coeff[i] + gain * acc)` -- so gain*acc agrees modulo 65536 too and the stored coefficient is bit-identical for every input.  No fixture can separate them, and `t_fpm_lmsupd`'s `acc_trunc_seen` guard, which does fire, only proves the truncation HAPPENS and not that it MATTERS.  So the 16-bit accumulator is settled by the object's `movswl %dx,%esi` at 0x0abdbd and by nothing this tier can do.  Recorded rather than deleted so the negative result is not re-derived; it expires if an instruction-level observable appears (tiers.md, F651).  This is the SECOND equivalent of exactly this shape found in one pass -- see fpmiirblock's `the section output is not narrowed`.
